{{Short description|Russian mathematician (born 1962)}}
'''Mikhail Kapranov''', (Михаил Михайлович Капранов, born 1962) is a Russian mathematician, specializing in [[algebraic geometry]], [[representation theory]], [[mathematical physics]], and [[category theory]]. He is currently a professor of the [[Kavli Institute for the Physics and Mathematics of the Universe]] at the [[University of Tokyo]].

Kapranov graduated from [[Lomonosov University]] in 1982 and received his doctorate in 1988 under the supervision of [[Yuri Manin]] at the [[Steklov Institute]] in Moscow.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id = 15018|title=Mikhail M. Kapranov}}</ref> Afterwards he worked at the Steklov Institute and from 1990 to 1991 at [[Cornell University]]. At [[Northwestern University]] he was from 1991 to 1993 an assistant professor, from 1993 to 1995 an associate professor, and from 1995 to 1999 a full professor. He was from 1999 to 2003 a professor at [[University of Toronto]] and from 2003 to 2014 a professor at [[Yale University]]. In 1993 he was a [[Sloan Research Fellow]]. From fall 2018 to spring 2019 he was a visiting professor at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Mikhail Kapranov|website=ias.org|url=https://www.ias.edu.org/scholars/mikhail-kapranov}}</ref>

From 1989 to 1990 he collaborated with [[Vladimir Voevodsky]] on <math>\infty</math>-groupoids, following the proposal made by [[Alexander Grothendieck]] in ''[[Esquisse d'un Programme]]''. In 1990 Voevodsky and Kapranov published “<math>\infty</math>-Groupoids as a Model for a Homotopy Category”,<ref>{{cite journal|author=Voevodsky, Vladimir Aleksandrovich|author2=Kapranov, Mikhail Mikhailovich|title=<math>\infty</math>-Groupoids as a model for a homotopy category|journal=Uspekhi Matematicheskikh Nauk|volume=45|issue=5|year=1990|pages=183–184|url=http://mi.mathnet.ru/eng/umn4790}}</ref> in which they claimed to provide a rigorous mathematical formulation and a logically valid proof of Grothendieck's idea connecting two classes of mathematical objects: <math>\infty</math>-groupoids and homotopy types. In October 1998, [[Carlos Simpson]] published on [[arXiv]] the article “Homotopy Types of Strict 3-groupoids”,<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Simpson, Carlos|title=Homotopy types of strict 3-groupoids|year=1998|eprint=math/9810059 }}</ref> which argued that the main result of the “<math>\infty</math>-groupoids” paper, published by Kapranov and Voevodsky in 1990, is false. It was not until 2013 Voevodsky convinced himself that Carlos Simpson's article is correct.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ias.edu/ideas/2014/voevodsky-origins|author=Voevodsky, Vladimier|year=2014|website=ias.org|title=The Origins and Motivations of Univalent Foundations: A Personal Mission to Develop Computer Proof Verification to Avoid Mathematical Mistakes}}</ref> Kapranov was also involved in the beginning of Voevodsky's program for the development of motivic cohomology.

With [[Israel Gelfand]] and [[Andrei Zelevinsky]], Kapranov investigated generalized Euler integrals, <math>A</math>-hypergeometric functions, <math>A</math>-discriminants, and hyperdeterminants, and authored ''Discriminants, Resultants, and Multidimensional Determinants'' in 1994.<ref>{{cite journal|author=Gel'fand, I.M.|author2=Kapranov, M.M.|author3=Zelevinsky, A.V.|title=Generalized Euler integrals and <math>A</math>-hypergeometric functions|journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]]|year=1990|volume=84|issue=2|pages=255–271|doi=10.1016/0001-8708(90)90048-R|doi-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|doi=10.1007/978-0-8176-4771-1_10|chapter=A-Discriminants|title=Discriminants, Resultants, and Multidimensional Determinants|pages=271–296|year=1994|last1=Gelfand|first1=Israel M.|last2=Kapranov|first2=Mikhail M.|last3=Zelevinsky|first3=Andrei V.|isbn=978-0-8176-4770-4}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|doi=10.1007/978-0-8176-4771-1_15|chapter=Hyperdeterminants|title=Discriminants, Resultants, and Multidimensional Determinants|pages=444–479|year=1994|last1=Gelfand|first1=Israel M.|last2=Kapranov|first2=Mikhail M.|last3=Zelevinsky|first3=Andrei V.|isbn=978-0-8176-4770-4}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|last=Roberts|first=David P.|date=2009|title=Review: Discriminants, Resultants, and Multidimensional Determinants, by I. M. Gelfand, M. M. Kapranov, and A. V. Zelevinsky|url=https://www.maa.org/press/maa-reviews/discriminants-resultants-and-multidimensional-determinants|archive-url=|archive-date=|access-date=1 Jul 2020|website=Mathematical Association of America}}</ref>

According to Gelfand, Kapranov, and Zelevinsky:
{{blockquote|... in an 1848 note on the resultant, [[Arthur Cayley|Cayley]] ... laid out the foundations of homological algebra. The place of discriminants in the general theory of hypergeometric functions is similar to the place of quasi-classical approximation in quantum mechanics. ... The relation between differential operators and their highest symbols is the mathematical counterpart of the relation between quantum and classical mechanics; so we can say that hypergeometric functions provide a "quantization" of discriminants.<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=2zgxQVU1hFAC&pg=PR9|chapter=Preface|page=ix|title = Discriminants, Resultants, and Multidimensional Determinants|isbn = 9780817647704|last1 = Gelfand|first1 = Israel M.|last2 = Kapranov|first2 = Mikhail|last3 = Zelevinsky|first3 = Andrei|date = 2008-04-16|publisher=Springer }} The note mentioned in the quotation is: {{cite journal|author=Cayley, Arthur|title=On the theory of elimination|journal=Cambridge and Dublin Mathematical Journal|issue=3|year=1848|pages=116–120|url=https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=mdp.39015030033925&view=1up&seq=128}}</ref>}}

In 1995 Kapranov provided a framework for a [[Langlands program]] for higher-dimensional schemes,<ref>{{cite book|author=Kapranov, Mikhail|chapter=Analogies between the Langlands correspondence and topological quantum field theory|editor=Gnidikin, S.|editor2=Lepowsky, J.|editor3=Wilson, R. L.|title=Functional Analysis on the Eve of the 21st century|publisher=Birkhäuser|year=1995|pages=119–151}}</ref> and with, [[Victor Ginzburg]] and Éric Vasserot, extended the "Geometric Langlands Conjecture" from algebraic curves to algebraic surfaces.

In 1998 Kapranov was an Invited Speaker with talk '' Operads and Algebraic Geometry '' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Kapranov, Mikhail|chapter=Operads and algebraic geometry|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=277–286|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011663000}}</ref>
